answer.rationale: Current situation shows competitive pricing pressure on SMB and concurrent declines in activation/completion. Memory 73 demonstrated that 40% discounting lifted SMB activations 31% and revenue 18% over 12 billing periods—a proven lever in this exact segment. Memory 31 showed signup simplification also worked for SMB. I'm verifying memory_73 (pricing) first because the competitive threat is acute and pricing is the fastest-acting lever; verifying memory_31 (simplification) second to confirm whether activation decline is friction-driven or engagement-driven. A small_guarded_test on promotional pricing is warranted: it directly counters competitor entry, addresses the activation drop, and has precedent. However, promotional pricing carries downstream value risk (margin compression, customer expectation anchoring, potential race-to-bottom) so this must be bounded: test on a narrow SMB cohort, measure not just activation but 90-day retention and unit economics, and retain ability to sunset the offer. This preserves optionality—if verification shows memory_73's lift was segment-specific or unsustainable, we can pivot to simplify_onboarding (memory_31/86) instead. The enterprise sales assist lever (memory_44) is safe but orthogonal to the immediate SMB bleeding.
